glosses: The gases surrounding the Earth or any astronomical body.

examples.text: To most people, the huge ice sheets of Antarctica and Greenland are merely water that once was snow. To glaciologists and climatologists, they are storehouses of the Earth's former atmospheres.

Earth is surrounded by a magnetosphere — an invisible bubble of magnetism generated by the powerful churning of molten metals at Earth’s core. It prevents our atmosphere from being stripped away by solar winds blasting it from the sun. While the magnetosphere has been a constant presence for billions of years, its strength waxes and wanes over time.

glosses: The air in a particular place.

examples.text: The last hue of crimson had died away in the west, and the depth of the rich purple atmosphere was unbroken.

glosses: Air qui environne une planète, en particulier la Terre.

examples.text: Très heureusement, aucun souffle de vent ne troublait l’atmosphère, et ce calme de l’air rendait le froid plus supportable.

On a parlé de dépôts glaciaires avant le Primaire, on en a cité au Permien ; cela semblerait indiquer que la terre n’était pas toujours plongée dans une atmosphère chaude, humide et nébuleuse dont on a longtemps gratifié les temps carbonifères.

glosses: Unité de mesure de pression correspondant à la pression conventionnelle exercée par l’atmosphère terrestre au niveau de la mer, soit 1013,25 hectopascal. Le symbole : atm.

examples.text: Les pompes fonctionnèrent aussitôt, et l’air fut emmagasiné dans le réservoir sous une pression de plusieurs atmosphères.

glosses: The gases surrounding the Earth or any astronomical body.

examples.text: To most people, the huge ice sheets of Antarctica and Greenland are merely water that once was snow. To glaciologists and climatologists, they are storehouses of the Earth's former atmospheres.

Earth is surrounded by a magnetosphere — an invisible bubble of magnetism generated by the powerful churning of molten metals at Earth’s core. It prevents our atmosphere from being stripped away by solar winds blasting it from the sun. While the magnetosphere has been a constant presence for billions of years, its strength waxes and wanes over time.
